title: Gas leak fire: source isolation, flashback and backdraft
summary: Fuel supply can be a control pathway, but the mechanism, equipment, residual gas and responsible professional role must be established. This source-only case provides evidence and gaps, not scene instructions.

conditions.title: Hot oxygen-starved enclosure containing unburned fuel
conditions.condition: A heated, oxygen-starved enclosure with substantial unburned fuel and possible ignition is reported; incoming air/mixing is relevant.
conditions.context_role: Descriptive condition; no automatic scene classification or operational approval.

intervention_basis.text: NIST documents a compartment backdraft mechanism involving air entry/mixing and ignition. It is distinct from upstream pipe flashback.
Responsible role: Qualified fire/incident professionals; source is a primary research report, not a scene protocol.

secondary_risks.text: A local flammable mixture can deflagrate and generate an extending flame/pressure wave.

gaps: Spatial temperature, oxygen and fuel-composition history
Geometry and scale matched to the actual enclosure

related_records.title: Related NASA BRE event: a command is not verified isolation
related_records.scope: A reviewed gas-emulator record distinguishes programmed fuel-flow termination from a confirmed natural-extinction event. It does not establish physical valve closure, measured release cessation, flashback protection or intervention performance.
limits: This is related laboratory/flight research, not a pressurized industrial leak or valve-system test.
Experimental measurements, command timestamps and raw bindings remain in the offline review.
A commanded stop does not independently establish flame persistence, valve closure, flow-off or post-shutdown reignition outcome.
External diffusion jet fire, upstream premixed/oxyfuel flashback and compartment backdraft are different mechanisms.
Neither valve closure always causes flashback nor valve closure always guarantees safety is established.
Visible flame extinction does not establish stopped leakage or atmosphere clearance.
Fuel isolation is a possible control pathway; the claim that only cooling or oxygen removal can control a gas fire is too broad.
Acetylene decomposition is a gas-specific exception; pure-fuel systems are not universally internally hazard-free.
UK/US guidance is cited within its stated scope, not automatically adopted as a local or ISS permission criterion.
No valve sequence, blanket deployment, DIY device instruction, actuator command or universal threshold is supplied.
NASA combustion records are related research; they do not qualify an industrial pipeline isolation system.
No fit, training, prediction or model validation is performed.
